title: Divide & Conquer
objective: Divide a curve into equal segments and mark every division with a circle.
learn: Curve operations, and how one component can output several kinds of data.

nodes.need: a component that splits a curve into a set number of equal parts
nodes.hint: Curve › Division. You want a fixed NUMBER of equal parts.
nodes.correct: Divide Curve splits a curve into N segments of equal length and returns three things: division Points, Tangents and parameters (t). Until Count is connected, N defaults to 10.

wrong.divideLength: Divide Length splits by a fixed distance, so the number of parts changes with the curve length. We want a set count.
wrong.shatter: Shatter cuts a curve at parameters you already have — we need to compute those first.
wrong.offset: Offset Curve makes a parallel copy; it doesn’t divide anything.
wrong.*: This slot needs a component that splits a curve into a set number of equal parts.

nodes.need: a component that draws a circle at each point
nodes.hint: Curve › Primitive. Round, with a plane and a radius.
nodes.correct: A point can act as a plane origin, so Circle runs once per division point: one list in, many circles out.

wrong.rectangle: Rectangle would place boxes — the challenge asks for circles marking each division.
wrong.pointParam: A Point parameter would just store the points again; nothing new is drawn.
wrong.pipe: Pipe needs a curve to follow; it wouldn’t mark individual points.
wrong.*: This slot needs a component that draws a circle at each point.

check.prompt: The Count slider should drive which input of Divide Curve?
check.hint: C = curve, N = number of segments, K = split at kinks.
check.correct: N is the number of segments. Drag Count and the points re-space themselves along the curve.

wrong.C: C expects the curve itself — it is already connected.
wrong.K: K is a True/False switch for splitting at kinks, not a count.

check.prompt: Which OUTPUT of Divide Curve should feed Circle’s P input?
check.hint: Circle needs locations. Which output holds positions in space?
check.correct: P outputs the division points. Each one becomes the centre of a circle.

wrong.T: T outputs tangent vectors — directions, not locations.
wrong.t: t outputs curve parameters — numbers along the curve, not points in space.
